source_documents.title: Constructing adaptive photosensitizers via supramolecular modification based on pillararene host−guest interactions

reference_evidence_units.quote: Est value of 0.2 eV, indicating a high intersystem crossing (ISC) rate for efficient ROS generation.
reference_evidence_units.subject: G
reference_evidence_units.statement: Separated HOMO/LUMO and small ΔEST predict fast ISC.

reference_evidence_units.quote: the consumption of ABDA was calculated to be 4.5 nmol
reference_evidence_units.subject: G
reference_evidence_units.statement: Efficient ROS (1O2) generation by G alone.

reference_evidence_units.quote: The TPE part not only endows G with aggregation-induced emission (AIE) property but also serves as an electron donor.
reference_evidence_units.subject: G
reference_evidence_units.statement: TPE gives AIE and acts as donor to the pyridinium acceptor.

reference_evidence_units.quote: Then photoinduced electron transfer (PET) happened between WP5 and G, resulting in the annihilating of the ROS generation
reference_evidence_units.subject: WP5⊃G complex
reference_evidence_units.statement: Host-to-guest PET switches ROS off in the complex.

reference_evidence_units.quote: the AIE molecule G itself showed very weak fluorescence in aqueous solution because of its good water solubility.
reference_evidence_units.subject: G
reference_evidence_units.statement: G alone is weakly emissive when dissolved.

reference_mechanisms.label: ICT_TICT_CT
reference_mechanisms.rationale: TPE donor / pyridinium acceptor separates the frontier orbitals to lower ΔEST (computation).

reference_mechanisms.label: TRIPLET_ISC_RTP_TADF
reference_mechanisms.rationale: G's photosensitizing ability is explained by fast ISC from a small ΔEST (computed), with ROS generation measured.

mechanism_decisions.label: RIM_RIR_RIV
mechanism_decisions.rationale: AIE is attributed to the TPE unit without naming restricted motion.

mechanism_decisions.label: PET_ET
mechanism_decisions.rationale: PET occurs between the WP5 host and G (E04); it belongs to the host-guest complex and is recorded out of pool.

out_of_pool: host-guest PET between WP5 and G quenches fluorescence and ROS; pH-driven shuttling restores them (E04)

reannotation.note: The paper's main switch is host-guest (out of pool; guideline §1.2 excludes host-defined systems). G's own in-pool mechanism is ISC; previous PET co_primary moved out of pool.
